name: Gypsy Home, Macharam
headline: A bed. A safer journey. A steadier childhood.
summary: Help provide beds, essential equipment and better access to care for a home in remote Macharam.
intro: For the children at Gypsy Home, a proper bed and a reliable way to reach care would make everyday life very different. Your support can help turn these basic needs into lasting comforts.
story: Balu and Jayamma run Gypsy Home in Macharam, a remote part of Mahabubnagar. The home cares for about 21 children and relies on people willing to reach a place that is not easy to find.

The field visit recorded children sleeping on floor mats, without beds or mattresses. The approach road and signage make access difficult. Management reported that the nearest hospital is around eight kilometres away, with no dedicated emergency vehicle.
The home also needs practical equipment for its kitchen, laundry, storage and learning. Steady support can help the carers plan for these essentials while continuing the work they already do.
needs: Beds and mattresses to replace sleeping on floor mats.
Emergency and regular transport options, with cycles for everyday mobility.
Kitchen equipment, a grinder, washing machine, hot water and clothing storage.
Computers, internet access and educational resources.
note: Transport options and equipment will be assessed before procurement. The ₹6 lakh target is an annual campaign goal, not a quoted item-wise budget.

name: Chayutha Ashramam
headline: Let the rain stay outside.
summary: Help repair a damaged roof, leaking water tank and essential facilities for about 25 boys.
intro: A roof should offer reassurance when it rains. Help Chayutha Ashramam repair the spaces that about 25 boys depend on every day.
story: Since 2002, Chayutha Ashramam has provided a home for boys in Wanaparthy. Srinivas Reddy Mitta runs the institution with local support, alongside wider food and community outreach.

The audit recorded openings and deterioration in the roof that allow rainwater inside. A leaking water tank adds another daily challenge. Management reported an estimated ₹1.5 lakh for the tank repair; the scope and cost still need confirmation.
Four washrooms need improvement, and the home also requires kitchen equipment and dining tables. Your contribution can help address these practical repairs and make everyday routines more dependable.
needs: Assess and repair the roof and shed where rainwater enters.
Verify and address the water-tank leakage and repair requirement.
Improve the condition of the four washrooms.
Kitchen equipment, a better cooking setup and dining tables.
note: The reported ₹1.5 lakh water-tank estimate is subject to confirmation. The overall ₹6 lakh annual target includes other documented needs; allocations will follow assessment.
photos: Roof openings and deterioration documented during the field visit.
Another view of the roof requiring attention.
The washroom area assessed during the visit.

name: Gnana Saraswathi Ashram
headline: Help strengthen the place they call home.
summary: Support a building assessment, better beds and improved washrooms for 10 boys.
intro: For ten boys, this ashram is part of everyday life. Help its carers address worn facilities and create a more comfortable place to grow.
story: Gnana Saraswathi Ashram in Nagarkurnool began in 2017 and is associated with Bhupal Reddy. The temple and daily Annadanam provide core support for the home, which currently accommodates ten boys.

During the visit, the team recorded wall cracks and maintenance concerns, around two washrooms, and older iron beds that need replacement. These are needs that deserve careful assessment and practical follow-through.

Computers and stronger medical linkages would also support the boys' development. Partial construction exists at the site; any construction support will depend on checking the documents, technical requirements and funding position.
needs: Technical inspection of visible cracking and a verified repair plan.
Replace old iron beds and improve bedding.
Assess and improve the limited washroom facilities.
Computer access and stronger links to medical support.
note: Construction and structural work are subject to technical assessment and document checks. The ₹6 lakh goal does not imply that a construction budget has already been verified.
photos: The common sleeping hall and existing iron beds.
Wall deterioration recorded during the assessment.
Visible wall cracking requiring technical inspection.

name: Meyers Balabhavan
headline: A window to a wider world. For 27 girls.
summary: Help a well-maintained home take its next step: access to computers and digital learning.
intro: A caring home is a beginning. Access to computers can open up new ways to learn, practise and imagine what comes next.
story: Meyers Balabhavan in Nalgonda has been operating since 2009 and currently accommodates 27 girls. It receives continuing support from St. Anne's, Visakhapatnam.
The field team found a clean, organised and well-maintained home, with established residential and dining facilities. Its identified requirement is specific: computers and digital learning.

This fundraiser focuses on that next step. Contributions can help build access to equipment and learning resources around an assessed plan, giving the girls more opportunities to explore, practise and develop digital confidence.
needs: Assess the number and specification of computers needed for shared learning.
Identify suitable educational tools and resources for the girls.
Plan how the equipment will be set up, maintained and used.
note: This fundraiser builds on the home's stable foundation by supporting digital learning. The ₹6 lakh annual target will follow a detailed equipment and learning plan.
photos: Meyers Balabhavan and its institutional signboard.

name: The Indian Gypsy Children Home
headline: Small comforts. A stronger childhood.
summary: Help 15 boys with safe water, better bedding, household equipment and learning resources.
intro: Clean drinking water. A comfortable bed. A place to keep your things. Help make these everyday comforts more dependable for fifteen boys in Suryapet.
story: Bhukya Dhanpal and his wife have maintained the Indian Gypsy Children Home since 2002. Today, fifteen boys live here. The home receives limited outside support and depends largely on local people and individual contributions.

The field assessment recorded small rooms in the older building and gaps in water, bedding, laundry, storage and educational equipment. The supplied photographs show the spaces the children use each day.

A new building is under construction but remains incomplete. This fundraiser prioritises practical, documented needs that can improve daily life, while any construction support will require further verification.
needs: A water purifier, improved sanitation and laundry support.
Better bedding, shelves, storage boxes and chairs.
A washing machine, mixer/grinder and basic kitchen equipment.
Computers, educational resources, sports equipment and growth-measurement tools.
note: Item-wise costs will be confirmed before procurement. Any support for the new building is subject to construction-document and funding checks.
photos: The home's premises and trust signboard in Suryapet.
The current arrangement for clothes and personal belongings.

name: Daiva Krupa Children Home
headline: Make everyday care more certain.
summary: Support recurring food grains, safe water, laundry equipment and storage for a locally supported home.
intro: Keeping a home running takes more than one act of kindness. Help turn occasional support into dependable essentials for the boys at Daiva Krupa.
story: Daiva Krupa Children Home, also shown as Dyva Krupa on its signboard, has operated in Mahabubabad for around twenty years. Management reports that the home depends on local support.

The assessment found a house-like, multi-level building with beds and mattresses in place. The immediate gaps are in recurring food supplies and everyday equipment: a water purifier, washing machine, racks and cupboards.
The number of current residents was not confirmed in the audit. What was clear was the need for stronger, steadier donor support so the home can plan for its basic requirements.
needs: Recurring food grains to support everyday meals.
A water purifier suited to the home's requirements.
A washing machine for regular household use.
Racks and cupboards for organised storage.
note: Current resident numbers and item-wise costs will be confirmed as the support plan is developed. The campaign target is ₹6 lakh for a year of documented needs.

name: Asha Bhavan Children's Home
headline: Eight beds. A place to belong.
summary: Help equip a planned girls' facility with eight beds and strengthen essentials across the home.
intro: A bed is a small space of your own. Help Asha Bhavan prepare eight beds for its planned girls' facility and meet the practical needs of a growing home.
story: Asha Bhavan Children's Home in Mahabubabad is operated by Empowering People Social Service Society. The audit recorded twenty boys in residence and outreach support reaching about fifty-four additional children.
A separate facility for girls is being arranged in a rented house. Management identified eight beds as an immediate requirement for that space.

The wider needs include a water purifier, washing machine, computers and ongoing operational support. Your contribution can help the team equip these spaces and build a steadier foundation for day-to-day care.
needs: Beds for the separate girls' facility being arranged in a rented house.
A water purifier and washing machine for everyday use.
Operational support matched to confirmed requirements.
note: Support for the planned girls' facility will follow confirmation of its readiness. Procurement and operational allocations will follow verification of current requirements.
